name: Piri Reis, world map, 1513 (surviving western fragment), Topkapı Palace Library, Istanbul
note: 2000x2753, a photograph of the parchment; the larger Commons files are the same photograph or other Piri Reis maps. The island is a solid red wash in mid-Atlantic between the Brazilian coast and Africa, about 67 x 87 px, ringed by red dots (the portolan convention for rocks and shoals) and lettered beside it; it is the story's plate. Its only known appearance, so the source was Etienne's from the start (October 2026).
extraction_note: --mode red, threshold 75, smooth 2, opening 3: 75-80 is a plateau at 66-67 x 86-87 px once the opening frees the dots that touch the east coast. At threshold 70 without the opening a rhumb line joins the southern dot and the island grows to 101 px tall. The dots are not kept.

fit_landmarks.name: Cabo de Sao Roque (where Brazil's coast turns south)

fit_note: Similarity fit on the first three: RMS 62 km, 4.05 km/px, rotation -9.5 deg, island centre [-35.0, 6.2]. With the Canaries added: RMS 173 km, 4.27 km/px, -5.8 deg, [-35.6, 6.1]. The two agree, and the rotation is modest, so unlike the Carta Marina or Mercator's Tuscia the fit is usable; the identifications of the Canaries and Cape Verde clusters are by position and drawing, not by legible names. An affine on the three is an extrapolation (barycentric weight -0.89) and is not used.
